output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the owner calls mintToken, the amount of tokens to be minted is added to the target's balance without a check, allowing the balance of the contract to become extremely large, and in turn, the owner's balance to become extremely large, causing a denial of service to users.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the balanceOf[_to] += _value; is executed, if _value is large enough, it can cause an overflow, making balanceOf[_to] to be a negative value, and in turn, allowing the owner of the corrupted account to transfer any amount of tokens from it, causing a denial of service to the owner.

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the balanceOf[_to] += _value; is executed, if _value is large enough, it can cause an overflow, making balanceOf[_to] to be a negative value, and in turn, allowing the owner of the corrupted account to transfer any amount of tokens from it, causing a denial of service to the owner.

The buy function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the amount = msg.value / buyPrice; is executed, if buyPrice is set to a very small value, attackers can call this function with a large msg.value, causing an overflow, and in turn, allowing attackers to buy arbitrary amount of tokens owned by the contract, causing a denial of service to the owner.
